description:
Cookies and Cream ice cream is one we ALWAYS get asked about so here it is. We have taken a tub of the OG Häagen Dazs Cookies & Cream and tried to see if it is still as good as it used to be.

The nice thing about Cookies and Cream ice cream is that it's dead easy to make. 

What you'll need:

500g Whipping Cream
500g Milk
180g Sugar
2 x Egg Yolks
50g Oreo vanilla cream (1 pack of Double Stuffed)
The remaining Oreo biscuits
10g Vanilla extract
50g SMP

As I said in the video, cookies and cream is made in many differernt ways so if you make yours differently, let us know in the comments below.

comments.text:
I've just discovered your channel and so far I'm loving watching every video. I noticed in some videos you simply use no fat skimmed milk powder, and in others you use other stabilisers? I thought you just used the milk powder in egg-less recipes, but here you use it also? Is there a simple rule to follow for knowing which stabiliser to use when?
Thanks! 
Luke from Canada
comments.author: @lukecohen4589

comments.text:
Hi Luke from Canada! Well you use skimmed milk powder to build solids content and create the preferred texture. Stabilizers are there to make the ice cream last longer, deal with ice crystals, freeze/thaw cycle, and to adjust viscosity and mouth feel. 
You can make good ice cream with just skimmed milk powder. You can make AMAZING ice cream by using skimmed milk powder WITH stabilizers. 
Where abouts in Canada are you?
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

I've tried different variations of this. I take double stuff cookies, and send them through the food processer. I make sure I get some does, and various "chunks". If I need to manually cut a cookie or two for bigger chunks, so be it. Freeze the results. I then do my vanilla base, churn it. Throw it in a bowl, then fold in the processed oreo cookies. 

Depending on the person I am making it for, I may do more or less, but I always put in a lot more cookie than what you've shown. There are also pie crusts in the states made of just oreos that I'll use to make an oreo ice cream pie - and those I'll do with about the same of what you've got shown here.
